en.sup: Supplied in English. The Greek verb has no object stated.

01.r: Sets out a case that may arise.
01.n: Abbott-Smith describes this particle as presenting something 'liable to happen' but not as definitely expected as with εἰ and the indicative.

02.r: Moves to the next step of the procedure.

03.r: He will not heed the witnesses brought to him.
03.n: Abbott-Smith gives older senses, 'to overhear' and 'to hear amiss or imperfectly', and a later one found in the Septuagint, where the verb renders, among others, Hebrew שָׁמַע, hear, with a negative. Here the context requires refusing to heed. An aorist subjunctive after 'if', a case that may or may not happen.

04.r: Those brought in at the earlier step of the procedure.
04.n: Who 'them' are is drawn from the procedure as a whole; the verse itself does not say.

05.r: A command to bring the matter before the community.
05.n: An aorist imperative, singular: addressed to the one who was wronged.

06.r: The article, in the dative case; 'to' comes from the case.

07.r: The gathered community of Jesus' followers.
07.n: Abbott-Smith derives the word from ἐκκαλέω, to call out, gives its proper sense as an assembly of citizens regularly convened, and notes that the Septuagint uses it chiefly for Hebrew קָהָל, the assembly of Israel. This study renders it 'assembly' here; the YLT does the same, the others say 'church'.

10.r: Marks the assembly as the last and weightiest voice.

11.r: The article, in the genitive case that this verb takes.

12.n: The Greek puts this word before the verb: 'if even the assembly he refuses to hear'.

14.r: A third-person command: this is how he is to stand.
14.n: A present imperative of the verb 'be', in the third person. The BSB's 'regard him' turns it into a command to the hearer.

15.r: In the hearer's own dealings with him.
15.n: Singular 'you', the brother who was wronged.

16.r: Compares how he is to be regarded.
16.n: Abbott-Smith defines it as 'just as, even as'.

17.r: Points to the Gentile as a type, not one particular man.

18.r: One outside the people of Israel.
18.n: Abbott-Smith's earlier senses are 'national' and 'foreign'; as a noun in the New Testament, 'the Gentile', citing this verse. He adds, in quotation marks, that the adjective 'describes character rather than mere position'.

20.r: The toll collector as a type.

21.r: A second figure the community kept at a distance.
21.n: This study renders the word 'toll collector' throughout. That the pairing with 'Gentile' means someone outside the fellowship is a reasonable reading of the verse; the text does not say what the treatment involves.
